fluff.overview:
The Javelin was introduced in 2751 by Stormvanger Assemblies as a light reconnaissance 'Mech designed for export to Star League member states. Built as a compromise between speed and firepower, the thirty-ton design proved fast enough to avoid heavier opponents while carrying sufficient weaponry to discourage pursuit. The Javelin's exceptional maneuverability made it equally adept at conducting ambushes, earning it the widespread reputation of appearing almost out of nowhere and giving rise to the phrase "sneaky as a Javelin."

Though production on Caph ended when the factory was destroyed during the Amaris Civil War in 2774, the Federated Suns (the design's largest customer) successfully incorporated the Javelin into virtually all of their BattleMech regiments. The design's continued popularity prompted Jalastar Aerospace to begin new production in 3055, ensuring the Javelin's service well into the thirty-second century.
fluff.capabilities:
The Javelin mounts a pair of Arrowlite SRM-6 launchers in its torso, providing devastating close-range firepower capable of exploiting breaches in enemy armor. With one ton of ammunition per launcher, the design carries sufficient missile stores for most engagements, though extended guerrilla operations can strain supply lines. The placement of these launchers so far forward in the torso creates a front-heavy center of gravity, giving the Javelin a distinctive forward lean when running at full speed. Pilots unfamiliar with this characteristic often struggle to keep the 'Mech upright in difficult terrain, though experienced MechWarriors learn to compensate for this tendency.

A GM 180 fusion engine propels the Javelin to speeds of ninety-seven kilometers per hour, while six Rawlings 95 jump jets provide a jumping distance of one hundred eighty meters. This mobility allows the Javelin to dictate engagements, closing rapidly to deliver its missile payload before withdrawing. However, with only four tons of StarGuard I armor, the design is ill-suited for prolonged firefights or hand-to-hand combat, and commanders typically withdraw their Javelins once ammunition is expended.
fluff.history:
Stormvanger Assemblies introduced the Javelin in 2751 as an export design for Star League member states seeking a capable light reconnaissance platform. The Federated Suns emerged as the largest customer, and House Davion took particular interest in the design's development. By the opening shots of the First Succession War, the Javelin had been integrated into most Federated Suns regiments, its sudden battlefield appearances catching many enemy combatants off guard.

The Javelin earned its reputation for ambush tactics during numerous engagements throughout the Succession Wars. During the long Battle of Kentares, a lance of Javelins and a Wasp from the Second Crucis Lancers executed a devastating rear attack against Kurita forces, destroying a Phoenix Hawk and damaging several other 'Mechs before using leapfrogging tactics to withdraw to friendly lines. The Second Battle of Cylene II in December 3002 demonstrated even more innovative usage, when recon lances composed mostly of Javelins hid beneath thirty meters of water in Waterhole Number Nine. When Kurita assault regiments entered the lake, the concealed Javelins surfaced and unleashed devastating point-blank missile barrages, contributing to the Combine's subsequent withdrawal from the planet.

The destruction of Stormvanger's Caph factory in 2774 during the Amaris Civil War ended original production. Despite this, the Javelin remained in widespread service, particularly with the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns. During the War of 3039, elements of the Tenth Deneb Light Cavalry on Marduk employed Javelins in aggressive anti-armor tactics, charging through Combine Demolisher formations while delivering full salvos of missiles.

Following the Clan Invasion, the Federated Commonwealth initiated upgrade programs incorporating recovered lostech. Jalastar Aerospace began producing new Javelins in 3055 at the behest of AFFC High Command, with the JVN-11D becoming the primary production variant during the Jihad era. The ilClan period has seen Jalastar return the Javelin to its classic missile-armed striker role with the JVN-12N, now featuring Clan-specification weaponry and enhanced mobility for continued service alongside Stingers and Wasps in AFFS reconnaissance lances.
fluff.deployment: Produced by Coalition Armory Inc. for the Filtvelt Coalition, this variant incorporates ferro-fibrous armor matching modern standards while accommodating the realm's technological limitations. Four Streak SRM-2 launchers provide ammunition-efficient firepower without overtaxing the single heat sinks that remain standard in Filtvelt's limited industrial base. The design demonstrates effective adaptation of the Javelin platform to peripheral state production capabilities.
